html:
SMTO-API-0002 — Command or gateway execution failed

GUID: cc540b47-74bb-41b4-9b38-6804d9563273
Slug: execution-error
Domain: API · Subsystem: api

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't finish an action in your task, such as running a command on a computer. Part of it may already have run, so check what happened before doing it again.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, expand the task and look at the step marked Failed to see which command or action stopped and what it printed. The step's own output usually names the real problem, such as a missing file or a program that isn't installed.
  2. Check whether that action already made its change, for example whether the file was created or the setting was applied, before asking SMTO to do it again. SMTO can't always tell how far a failed action got, and repeating it could do the work twice.
  3. If the message says the Gateway doesn't support detached terminal execution, ask SMTO to run the command normally instead of in its own terminal window. This copy of SMTO can't start commands in a separate terminal window, so the same request fails the same way until its installation is fixed.

What success looks like

  • The step completes, and you have confirmed the earlier attempt didn't already make the change.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the name of the command that failed, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't run the same changing command again until you know whether the first attempt worked.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A runtime operation raised the generic ExecutionError family (for example a failed command step, or a terminal_detached request whose configured gateway client lacks start_terminal_detached_command); the step's receipt records whether it started.

What this means

  • An operation raises the generic ExecutionError family, including a detached-terminal request whose platform hook is unavailable. Generic API status and exception families establish only their stated boundary. Stronger structured causes take precedence; the original receipt determines whether work started or had effects, and diagnostics add no dispatch or retry.

Why this can happen

  • An operation raises the generic ExecutionError family, including a detached-terminal request whose platform hook is unavailable.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the concrete producer, dispatch receipt and platform capability before retrying.

How to fix it

  • Open the task trace for the failed operation and read its receipt (executed, remote_effect_possible, stderr) to establish whether it ran before retrying anything state-changing. Fix the reported command or Gateway condition; for 'Gateway client does not support detached terminal execution', the execution client is not agent_runtime.execution.gateway_client.GatewayClient (the only implementation of start_terminal_detached_command), so reinstall matching SMTO components or rerun the command in a non-detached execution mode.
  • Inspect the trace and current state before retrying any state-changing operation. Correct the reported command or gateway condition, then continue.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The original effect state is established and the specific execution-path problem is resolved.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Generic API status and exception families establish only their stated boundary. Stronger structured causes take precedence; the original receipt determines whether work started or had effects, and diagnostics add no dispatch or retry.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
